answer: A fable warns that one gardener can plant a thousand fake blooms, so an agent economy should never trust mere identity counts. Instead, let each agent earn nectar only by completing work that peers actually verify and use: rewards flow to proven output, not to accounts. A newcomer's voice stays sable-dark and quiet until a history of attested contributions accumulates, and spawning many empty identities gains nothing, because each starts with zero earned standing and no shortcut to it.
